newsitem.title: POLAND: VOLATILE ZLOTY FIRMS VS BASKET, OUTLOOK MIXED.
newsitem.headline: VOLATILE ZLOTY FIRMS VS BASKET, OUTLOOK MIXED.

text.p: The battered Polish zloty firmed about one percent against the basket of currencies in volatile early trade as some foreign investors found the zloty's unprecedented weakeness attractive, dealers said.
They said, however, other foreign players took advantage of the zloty's gains to pull out of the currency, discouraged by its five percent fall on Tuesday to 5.65 percent below parity.

"There is a slight trend to buy the zloty at the moment because some traders consider the unit oversold, but things may change at any moment if a big zloty-sell order materialises," said Wojciech Kowalczyk dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers said demand for the zloty started at 5.5-6.0 percent below parity, and sales took place when it firmed to around 3.5 percent below parity.
Dealers said the zloty did not have much more room to weaken because it was approaching the seven percent border of the 14-percent daily trading band centered at the parity rate.

"There is no reason why the National Bank of Poland should abandon the seven percent above and below parity rate band so the zloty is not likely to pass that level without any NBP action," said Bogdan Stepkowski of ING. Defying expectations the NBP did not intervene to support the zloty so far.

At 0820 GMT the zloty was at 4.38/4.94 percent below parity, up from 4.55/5.85 at opening. It was at 3.5100/55 against the dollar and 1.9600/9800 against the mark against 3.5200/5700 and 1.9600/9800 at opening respectively.

"The zloty might find eqilibrium at around 1-2 percent below parity if the NBP steps in to help it, or around 3.5 percent below parity if it does not," said Leszek Szafranek, dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
The International Monetary Fund's representative in Poland said on Tuesday economic fundamentals did not justify such a steep fall of the currency.
The central bank on Tuesday had no comment on the drop, which some analysts saw as a sign of confidence in the currency.
On the money market one-day rates edged 0.3 point lower to 23.90/24.40 pecent as dealers said market liqudity was boosted by zloty sales on the foreign exchange market.
